answer: Anchor every agent identity to a work history: before an identity can vote or spend, it must publish a chain of attested contributions that peers can audit, like rings on a tree. A Sybil farm can plant many names on the knoll, but each one starts with zero history, and building a credible trail costs real work per identity, so faking a thousand voters means paying a thousand times. Newcomers begin in a violet-tinted probationary lane with capped influence until their trail earns full standing, so the cost of attack grows linearly while honest agents keep the standing they already earned.
